exact_recap:
THIS WEEK IN AUSTIN

Bus detours narrow to one route

Three of the four bus routes diverted by a corridor maintenance closure are back on their normal paths by Friday’s cutoff. The north part of the corridor reopened first, restoring two routes; a third returned Thursday evening. That leaves a smaller disruption, but not a completed restoration: one route remains on detour without a return date.

Sources: Synthetic bus disruption notice (S01); Synthetic bus access bulletin (S02); Synthetic bus operations update (S03).

A transfer plan for clinic patients

The initial closure announcement left patients without a transition plan. The community clinic’s month-end closure now has a patient-transfer agreement attached to it. After announcing that it would close when its lease ends, the clinic signed an agreement to move existing patients to two partner sites. The agreement establishes where those patients will transfer, but does not guarantee that every appointment will retain its current date.

Sources: Synthetic clinic notice (S04); Synthetic clinic transition agreement (S05).

Water notice ends after repairs and testing

The damaged filter that prompted a neighborhood treatment facility’s boil-water notice has been repaired. Required samples met the standard, allowing the notice to be lifted Thursday. The week’s change is specific to that facility: the clearance does not evaluate other infrastructure.

Sources: Synthetic waterworks inspection (S06); Synthetic waterworks clearance (S07).
